correctness.rationale: A labelled one-point extension is exactly a matching in the leave. If F has rows of uncovered-site indicators, K=FF^T and the row lattice is generated by the all-ones vector and the edge-sums: subtract single-edge rows from the empty row, and express every matching row in those generators. A surjection from Z^m onto this free row lattice splits, giving a unimodular row basis and an integral congruence to its Gram matrix plus a zero block. Along an edge the quotient identifies the endpoints up to sign, so a connected edge-sum quotient is Z/2 in the nonbipartite case and Z via signed sum in the bipartite case. An odd-size nonbipartite component with connected leave gives the unimodular lattice after adding all ones; for connected even n the two distinct order-two discriminant classes of D_n are represented by e_1 and half the all-ones vector. The balanced bipartite lattice becomes A_(n-1) via a coordinate sign change and has cyclic discriminant of order n. For imbalance s>0 the lattice has index s and dual obtained by adjoining the sign vector divided by s. The discriminant group has order s^2, generators a,b and relations sa=0, sb=na, hence the claimed gcd and complementary factors. The single vertex gives [1]. Componentwise rational spans miss one dimension per bipartite component; adding the single all-ones vector raises the rank by exactly one iff a bipartite component is unbalanced. Direct independent matching enumeration and exact Smith reduction of the full overlaps reproduced both named examples and odd/even nonbipartite and disconnected examples. K is positive semidefinite by the Gram factorization; this does not assert joint realizability of the extension diagrams.
residual_risks: The disconnected statement gives rank and an algorithm rather than closed invariant factors by component data. The kernel does not count two-point amalgams or concern complete first-order types.
